process_correction: All code changes go through Builder. Lead only reads, runs gates, greps, and edits openspec/ + AGENTS.md.

committed.message: feat: lazy file transfer protocol v0.4 (Phases 1-5)

offer_fanout_verified.delivered: broadcast_offer fanning out to already-connected peers, filtered on the recipient's lazy-file capability, sender skipped; 5 tests
offer_fanout_verified.capability_filter_confirmed: hub.rs:1057 skips a peer whose caps lack LAZY_FILE, which also excludes every pre-0.4 client for free since their capability set is empty
offer_fanout_verified.builders_borrow_correction: my snippet moved `offer` into the map and then tried to clone from it; it restructured to copy file_id, clone the frame, then move -- my version would not have compiled
offer_fanout_verified.known_gap_it_flagged: a full routed-frame buffer drops the offer notification for that peer with only a warn. The offer itself stays in the map and remains pullable, and it reappears in welcome.offers on reconnect -- the same trade-off broadcast_abort already makes. Not addressed; adding retry needs per-peer offer versioning.

second_unimplemented_requirement_found.spec_text: A sender SHALL publish offers only when the hub advertises `lazy-file`
second_unimplemented_requirement_found.reality: transport.rs parses hub_caps at line 455 but uses it only for a debug line and a consistency warning; it is never handed to the supervisor, and publish_offers looks only at SendMode
second_unimplemented_requirement_found.consequence: a v0.4 client with send_mode=lazy against a v0.3 hub publishes offers into the void. The v0.3 hub ignores unknown frame types by design, so nothing errors -- the copy looks successful and no peer can ever pull it. Silent failure.
second_unimplemented_requirement_found.fix_dispatched: hub_caps becomes a watch::Receiver on Transport so reconnects are visible; SendPolicy::may_publish_offers requires both the local mode and the hub capability; when lazy is configured but the hub cannot act on it, fall back to eager with a single warning per connection rather than failing the copy
second_unimplemented_requirement_found.judgement_called_out: the spec does not say whether to degrade or fail. I chose degrade because the user's intent is to send the file and eager is the known-good v0.5.4 path; refusing would leave them unable to copy anything with no actionable fix. The builder may argue otherwise but must justify it.
